io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException: Failed to encode packet clientbound/minecraft:level_particles
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft snapshot 24w13a.  
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.  
3. Open the chat window and enter the command ``/particle minecraft:item minecraft:air``.  
4. Observe that the client crashes (the game disconnects and an error similar to “Failed to encode packet clientbound/minecraft:level_particles” appears).
Observed Behavior: When the command /particle minecraft:item minecraft:air is executed, or when an area‑effect‑cloud is summoned with its Particle NBT tag set to “minecraft:item minecraft:air”, the server attempts to send a level_particles packet containing an ItemStack that has no item data. The packet encoder encounters an empty ItemStack, throws an EncoderException stating that an empty ItemStack is not allowed, and the packet fails to be written to the client. This failure propagates through the Netty pipeline, resulting in a server‑side error log that reports “Error sending packet clientbound/minecraft:level_particles” followed by a stack trace ending with “Failed to encode packet clientbound/minecraft:level_particles”. Because the client never receives a valid particle packet, the connection is terminated and the player is disconnected with an internal exception indicating the same encoder failure. The crash occurs consistently on 24w13a and any version that includes the same particle handling code.
Expected Behavior: When the command /particle minecraft:item minecraft:air is executed, or an area effect cloud is created with its Particle tag set to “minecraft:item minecraft:air”, the game should accept the command, send the particle packet without error, and simply render no visible particle (or treat the empty ItemStack as a no‑op). The client should remain stable and stay connected.
